1. A robot motion control method, applied to a robot, the method comprising:
obtaining a center-of-mass reference trajectory for guiding the robot to execute a target motion;
the center-of-mass reference trajectory being a center-of-mass motion trajectory of the robot configured to achieve the target motion;
obtaining, based on optimization of an objective function, center-of-mass control information for controlling the robot to follow the center-of-mass reference trajectory to move;
generating joint control information according to the center-of-mass control information and a structure matrix of the robot; and
controlling the robot to execute the target motion based on the joint control information.
2. The method according to claim 1, wherein a value of the objective function is representing a degree of deviation of the robot from the center-of-mass reference trajectory, and the obtaining the center-of-mass control information for controlling the robot to follow the center-of-mass reference trajectory to move comprises:
obtaining desired center-of-mass motion data of the robot based on the center-of-mass reference trajectory, the desired center-of-mass motion data being a desired value of motion data associated with a center of mass of the robot; and
calculating, based on the desired center-of-mass motion data, the center-of-mass control information enabling the value of the objective function to satisfy an optimization stop condition.

4. The method according to claim 2, wherein the calculating the center-of-mass control information comprises:
utilizing quadratic programming (QP) optimization to calculate the center-of-mass control information.
5. The method according to claim 2, wherein the calculating the center-of-mass control information comprises:
utilizing interior point optimizer (IPOPT) optimization to calculate the center-of-mass control information.
6. The method according to claim 2, wherein the obtaining the desired center-of-mass motion data of the robot based on the center-of-mass reference trajectory comprises:
obtaining actual center-of-mass motion data of the robot;
obtaining reference center-of-mass motion data of the robot according to the center-of-mass reference trajectory;
obtaining a center-of-mass motion data adjustment value according to a difference between the actual center-of-mass motion data and the reference center-of-mass motion data; and
obtaining the desired center-of-mass motion data according to the center-of-mass motion data adjustment value and the reference center-of-mass motion data.
7. The method according to claim 6, wherein the obtaining the center-of-mass motion data adjustment value according to the difference between the actual center-of-mass motion data and the reference center-of-mass motion data comprises:
calculating a difference between the actual center-of-mass motion data and the reference center-of-mass motion data; and
obtaining the center-of-mass motion data adjustment value according to a gain matrix and the difference, the gain matrix corresponding to the motion data associated with the center of mass of the robot.
8. The method according to claim 6, wherein the center-of-mass motion data adjustment value comprises a center-of-mass acceleration adjustment value and a center-of-mass angular acceleration adjustment value.
9. The method according to claim 8, wherein the center-of-mass acceleration adjustment value is represented by padj = Kd(pref_pact) + Kp(prefpact) where padj denotes a center-of-mass acceleration adjustment value, pref denotes a reference center-of-mass velocity, pact denotes an actual center-of-mass velocity, pref denotes a reference center-of-mass position, pact denotes an actual center-of-mass position, Kd and Kp denote gain matrices associated with center-of-mass acceleration.
10. The method according to claim 8, wherein the center-of-mass angular acceleration adjustment value is represented by 6adj = Kd(oref-act) + Kp(RrefRact)v, where 6adj denotes a center-of-mass angular acceleration adjustment value, oref denotes a reference center-of-mass angular velocity, oact denotes an actual center-of-mass angular velocity, Rref denotes a reference rotation matrix of a center-of-mass coordinate system relative to a world coordinate system, Ract denotes an actual rotation matrix of the center-of-mass coordinate system relative to the world coordinate system, (RrefRact)v denotes a rotation vector from Ract to Rref, and Kp and Kd denote gain matrices associated with center-of-mass angular acceleration.
11. The method according to claim 1, wherein the method further comprises:
performing kinetics analysis on a particle model to obtain a kinetics equation, the particle model being obtained by simplification based on a robot body; and
analyzing the kinetics equation and constructing the objective function based on an objective of making the center-of-mass motion trajectory of the robot consistent with the center-of-mass reference trajectory.
12. The method according to claim 1, wherein the generating the joint control information according to the center-of-mass control information and the structure matrix of the robot comprises:
generating intermediate joint control information according to the center-of-mass control information and the structure matrix corresponding to the robot;
obtaining actual joint motion data of the robot;
obtaining reference joint motion data of the robot; and
adjusting the intermediate joint control information according to the actual joint motion data and the reference joint motion data to obtain the joint control information.
13. The method according to claim 12, wherein the joint control information comprises joint torque represented by T = -Jfopt + K (grefpact) + Kp(grefgact), where T denotes joint torque, J, denotes the structure matrix corresponding to the robot, fopt denotes the center-of-mass control information obtained by optimization, gref denotes a reference joint angular velocity, gact denotes an actual joint angular velocity, gref denotes a reference joint angle, qact denotes an actual joint angle, and Kp and Kd are gain matrices associated with the joint torque.
14. The method according to claim 13, wherein the robot is a quadruped robot, and the target motion is a motion process from a four-legged lying down state to a two-legged standing state.
